MLuDL-TlJgg.context: Released July 22, 2022, 'Chant' marked Macklemore's first single of the year and served as the lead single for his third solo album Ben (2023). Thematically rooted in personal resurrection — addressing his near-fatal drug overdose in 2020, career self-doubt during the pandemic, and a defiant refusal to retire — the video channels those themes through gospel-inflected visuals shot in Seattle landmarks. The collaboration with Australian pop phenomenon Tones and I (whose 'Dance Monkey' reached No. 4 on the Hot 100) gave the track transatlantic reach. The Seattle setting, including Saint Mark's Episcopal Cathedral and Memorial Stadium, grounds the video in Macklemore's long-established Pacific Northwest identity and community-first ethos.
MLuDL-TlJgg.curatorial: High curatorial value as a document of Macklemore's artistic reinvention after a five-year solo album hiatus and personal health crisis. The video's use of Seattle civic spaces, a gospel choir, and community participation gives it ethnographic significance as a record of the city's music culture. Its deliberate visual austerity — low saturation, high contrast, rain-drenched environments — makes it a strong aesthetic counterpoint to the maximalist visual language dominant in hip-hop video product
MLuDL-TlJgg.sig: Represents a 2020s evolution of confessional hip-hop, blending rap with gospel choir, piano-driven production, and stadium-scale communal imagery. Signals a shift away from hip-hop maximalism toward introspective, spiritually-coded visual language — a notable departure from the high-saturation, high-energy aesthetic of early 2010s mainstream rap video production.

Jyw0ZYRflWI.context: Released March 2023 as Liyah Katana's introductory major-label single, 'STR8' positions a 19-year-old Mississauga-born artist as part of a new generation of Canadian R&B talent signed to the storied Def Jam label via No I.D.'s ARTium Records imprint. The video arrives during a broader post-pandemic moment of Toronto R&B visibility, with the city producing a wave of vocally-driven, introspective artists recalling the emotional directness of early-2000s R&B. The lakeside retreat setting, candlelight aesthetic, and live string element signal a deliberate push toward elevated, mood-forward visuals in contrast to trend-driven commercial R&B of the period.
Jyw0ZYRflWI.curatorial: High curatorial value as a documented debut major-label visual for a Def Jam-signed Canadian R&B artist. The video is a clean example of the intimate, realism-grounded aesthetic favored by emerging neo-soul and contemporary R&B acts in the early 2020s. Its notable commercial traction (500K YouTube views, SoundCloud Top 50 R&B chart peak) and critical recognition from Complex Canada make it a meaningful archival marker of the Toronto R&B scene's rising international profile during this period.
Jyw0ZYRflWI.sig: Represents the 2020s neo-soul and contemporary R&B revival, particularly the Canadian wing, drawing lineage from artists like Jill Scott, Musiq Soulchild, and early Brandy. The song's piano-driven production and raw breakup narrative place it squarely in the post-SZA introspective R&B tradition, while Katana's vocal approach nods to church-rooted gospel expressiveness.

The song's themes of self-loss in a toxic relationship resonated strongly with a TikTok-native audience already primed by 'Good Looking,' bridging Waterhouse's cult indie following with mainstream streaming visibility.
